howIBuild.title: How I build products
howIBuild.description: I'm not just a dev who writes code. I think product, architecture and business — from problem to production-ready solution.

1.title: Problem discovery
1.description: Before writing a single line of code, I understand the real problem. I talk to users, analyze market context and define which pain needs to be solved — and whether it's worth solving.

2.title: Product hypothesis
2.description: I turn the problem into a testable hypothesis: 'If we build X for Y, outcome Z will happen.' This hypothesis guides all scope and priority decisions.

3.title: MVP definition
3.description: I cut everything not essential to validate the hypothesis. The MVP needs to be small enough to ship fast and large enough to generate real learning.

4.title: Technical architecture
4.description: I choose the stack and define the structure before coding. I think about scalability, maintainability and operational cost — not just what works right now.

5.title: Design system
5.description: I create or adapt a design system before building screens. Consistent components save time, reduce UI bugs and make the product more visually cohesive.

6.title: Frontend development
6.description: I build interfaces with Next.js, TypeScript and TailwindCSS. I prioritize performance, accessibility and user experience — not just appearance.

7.title: Backend development
7.description: I implement business logic, APIs, authentication and database. I use Prisma, PostgreSQL and Redis to have full control over data and application state.

8.title: AI integration
8.description: When it makes sense, I add AI layers: RAG for contextual search, LLMs for content generation, embeddings for recommendations. AI enters as a lever, not as hype.

9.title: Deploy and observability
9.description: Deployment on VPS with Docker and EasyPanel. I configure logs, metrics and alerts to have real visibility into what happens in production — no surprises.

10.title: Iteration based on feedback
10.description: After launch, I monitor metrics, collect feedback and iterate. A launched product that learns is worth far more than a perfect product that never ships.
